hints: Focus on the functional groups needed for esterification, not just the carbon skeletons.
Remember an ester forms from a carboxylic acid, with $\text{-COOH}$, plus an alcohol, with $\text{-OH}$.
Scan each pair for one molecule with $\text{C(=O)OH}$ and the other with $\text{C-OH}$, then pick the pair that has both.
walkthrough:
**Recall how esters are made**

Esters are made by esterification, a condensation between a carboxylic acid and an alcohol with loss of water. Think acid plus alcohol gives ester plus water.

$$\text{R-COOH} + \text{R'-OH} \rightleftharpoons \text{R-COOR'} + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$

**Identify the functional group in each molecule**

Look for $\text{-OH}$ attached to C for an alcohol, $\text{C=O}$ in the middle of a chain for a ketone, $\text{-CHO}$ at the end for an aldehyde, and $\text{-COOH}$ for a carboxylic acid. Only the acid plus alcohol combination works.

**Check each pair and conclude**

Only one pair contains a $\text{-COOH}$ group on one molecule and a $\text{C-OH}$ group on the other. That pair can condense to form an ester linkage, $\text{-COO-}$, so it is the correct choice.

options.A: Incorrect. This is butan-2-ol (a secondary alcohol) plus butan-2-one (a ketone). Ketones do not react with alcohols to give esters under normal esterification conditions.
options.B: Incorrect. This is butan-1-ol (a primary alcohol) plus butanal (an aldehyde). An aldehyde plus an alcohol can form a hemiacetal or acetal, not an ester.
options.C: Correct. This is propane-1,2,3-triol (glycerol, with three alcohol $\text{-OH}$ groups) plus 2-methylpropanoic acid (with $\text{-COOH}$). Carboxylic acid plus alcohol undergoes esterification to give an ester plus water.
options.D: Incorrect. This is butanal (an aldehyde) plus butanoic acid (a carboxylic acid). There is no alcohol present, so no esterification can occur. Students sometimes confuse aldehydes with alcohols because both contain oxygen.
